title: Notifications contract
description: Language-neutral notification shapes shared by iOS, Android, backend, and admin. notification mirrors the Firestore `notifications/{uid}/items/{notificationId}` document: owner-only read, backend-only write (delivery via the backend writer, read-state via notifications.markRead / markAllRead). Push token registrations store ONLY the SHA-256 hash of the FCM token (the hash is the document ID); the raw token never appears in documents, logs, or responses. Retention (scheduled cleanup): unread items 30 days, read items 7 days. Preferences live in the owner-writable `userPrivate/{uid}.notificationPreferences` map; the essential account-notice categories (account_warning, account_suspension) cannot be disabled — enforced at delivery time by the backend writer, which is the sole inbox author. Firestore stores timestamps as native Timestamp values; this contract describes their ISO 8601 JSON serialization.

notificationCategory.description: Active categories only. The legacy contract's future categories (partner_offer, event_chat, nearby_event) must not be sent without product and security review and are deliberately excluded. event_created is a producer-only community broadcast: the events-onEventPublished Firestore trigger fans it out to every active member (minus the creator) when an event becomes published, deep-linking to the event on tap; it is NOT admin-sendable. The social categories (direct_message, community_chat, convoy_chat, friend_request, convoy_invite) carry member-to-member activity for the chat/social features; they are all optional (never essential) so a user can always silence other members, and activating any of them as a delivery surface requires the same product/security review. Only convoy_invite has a producer today — the others are preference-only until their domains wire one up.

adminSendableCategory.description: The subset of notificationCategory that notifications.adminSend accepts — deliberately narrower than notificationCategory. The social categories describe activity between members, so accepting one from an admin broadcast would let it impersonate a DM, friend request, or convoy invite the recipient never received. Social notices are producer-only.

notification.description: Firestore `notifications/{uid}/items/{notificationId}`. Owner-only read; no client writes. Plain text only — no HTML. List newest-first by createdAt; unread count via an aggregate count query on read == false.

previewText.description: Swedish preview text. Must not contain protected details.

batchId.description: Producer batch/idempotency marker for grouped sends.

notificationPreferenceEntry.description: Per-category entry in `userPrivate/{uid}.notificationPreferences` (owner-writable map, category → entry). Missing entries default to enabled. The essential categories ignore inApp=false at delivery time.

markNotificationReadRequest.description: Input for notifications.markRead. Ownership is structural — the callable only touches the caller's own inbox, so another user's notification ID is not-found. Idempotent.

marked.description: False when the notification was already read (idempotent replay).

registerPushTokenRequest.description: Input for notifications.registerPushToken (active users; gated by the pushNotifications flag). The raw token is hashed server-side and never stored.

tokenId.description: SHA-256 hex of the token — also the pushTokens document ID. Re-registering the same token returns the same tokenId (idempotent).

unregisterPushTokenRequest.description: Input for notifications.unregisterPushToken. Requires authentication only — suspended users may clean up their devices. Idempotent.

pushTokenRegistration.description: Firestore `userPrivate/{uid}/pushTokens/{tokenId}` where tokenId is the SHA-256 hex of the raw FCM token. One document per device, so a member may hold several. NO client access at all (read included) — the document carries the raw, send-addressable FCM token, which only the Admin SDK needs; the client learns its own token from the FCM SDK. All writes go through the register/unregister callables. Erased with userPrivate/{uid} on account deletion. Dead tokens (FCM UNREGISTERED / INVALID_ARGUMENT) are pruned by the notifications-onNotificationCreated send path.

token.description: Raw FCM registration token. Required to send — FCM addresses a device by the token itself. Never logged, never returned by a callable, never client-readable.
